Dear Dr. Miller,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate Julian Vance, a 12-year-old male who presented to my clinic for a comprehensive routine evaluation. He is generally thriving, doing well in the seventh grade, and is taking no regular medications. His height and weight are both tracking along the 50th percentile, and family medical history is non-contributory.

On physical examination, Julian has a distinctly circular facial contour with full cheeks, and his auricles are situated notably inferior to the horizontal line connecting the inner canthi. An oral inspection revealed an accessory projection along the lingual aspect of his maxillary incisor consistent with a prominent retroform cusp. Notably, he exhibits a complete complement of permanent dentition without any missing teeth, and tooth size is typical, with no unusually small crowns observed.

Examination of the upper extremities is notable for bilaterally abducted thumbs showing marked hyperextension at the interphalangeal joints. In addition, there is radial incurvature of his fifth digits. Plain radiographs of the hands, obtained previously after a minor sports injury, confirmed the presence of an extra phalangeal segment within the second digits bilaterally. 

The rest of Julian's general examination was unremarkable; his chest is clear to auscultation, cardiovascular sounds are normal without murmurs, abdomen is soft and non-tender, and his neurologic exam and gait are intact. 

I would be grateful for your expert clinical assessment regarding this constellation of craniofacial, dental, and digital findings. Please let me know your thoughts or if any further diagnostic workup is warranted.

Warm regards,

Dr. Evelyn Reed
Riverside Pediatric Clinic
